subskill: Integer solutions of a compound inequality with a constant
prompt:
3k - 7 < 11 - 7x ≤ 60
In the compound inequality above, k is a constant. For how many integer values of k does the inequality have at least 3 negative integer solutions and more negative integer solutions than positive integer solutions?
explanation: Solve each part for x. From 11 - 7x ≤ 60, -7x ≤ 49, so x ≥ -7 (dividing by -7 reverses the sign, and -7 itself IS a solution because the original sign was ≤). From 3k - 7 < 11 - 7x, 7x < 18 - 3k, so x < (18 - 3k)/7; call this bound U. It is strict, so U itself is never a solution. The solutions are the integers x with -7 ≤ x < U. Case 1, k ≤ 8: then U > -1, so all seven negative integers -7, ..., -1 are solutions (at least 3, as required), and there must be at most 6 positive solutions, so 7 must NOT be a solution: U ≤ 7, which gives 18 - 3k ≤ 49, k ≥ -31/3, so k ≥ -10. That is k = -10, ..., 8: 19 values. Case 2, k ≥ 9: then U ≤ -3, so there are no positive solutions (and 0 is not a solution), and the negatives run from -7 up to below U. At least 3 of them means -5 must be a solution: -5 < U, which gives 18 - 3k > -35, k < 53/3, so k ≤ 17. That is k = 9, ..., 17: 9 values. Total: 19 + 9 = 28. (Having some solution at all only needs k ≤ 22; the requirement of at least 3 negative solutions is what stops the count at k = 17.) Choice 23 comes from reversing the inequality but carrying the 'or equal' to the wrong end (x > -7 and x ≤ U). Choice 26 counts 0 as a positive solution. Choice 19 stops after Case 1 and misses the values of k for which there are no positive solutions but still at least 3 negative ones.
solve: let n=0; for (let k=-200;k<=200;k++){ let neg=0,pos=0; for (let x=-100;x<=100;x++){ const m=11-7*x; if (m<=60 && 3*k-7<m){ if(x<0)neg++; else if(x>0)pos++; } } if (neg>=3 && neg>pos) n++; } return n;

second branch: no positives, at least 3 negatives
